subject: social
topic: Minutes of scrolling idealised bodies changes how you see your own
angle: Viewing idealized and manipulated images on social media causes lower body satisfaction, particularly for younger people with a tendency to compare themselves to others.
title: The Cost of the Perfect Feed

hooks.text: Whose body are you measuring yourself against?
You see the edit, but you do not see the change.
You are letting manipulated images dictate your worth.
A thumb moves over a glass screen in a dark room.

reveal.headline: Manipulated photos are rated more positively than original ones.
reveal.body: Even when the reshaping of bodies is not noticed well, the edited image is preferred.

explain.headline: Social media exposure lowers body satisfaction.
explain.body: Viewing manipulated Instagram photos directly leads to lower body image in girls aged 14–18. This effect is stronger for those with high social comparison tendencies.

matters.headline: Internalizing these ideals changes your self-perception.
matters.body: Internalization of body shape ideals is strongly linked to body dissatisfaction in younger individuals. That may be why your self-image shifts after scrolling.

example.headline: A late night scroll in bed.
example.body: You lie in the dark and look at thin media images. Your reflection in the mirror feels different the next morning.

question.headline: Whose body are you comparing yours to?

claims.text: Manipulated photos were rated more positively than original photos, even though the reshaping of the bodies was not noticed very well.
claims.quote: Interestingly, the manipulated photos were rated more positively than the original photos. Although the use of filters and effects was detected, reshaping of the bodies was not noticed very well.

claims.text: Exposure to manipulated Instagram photos directly leads to lower body image in girls aged 14–18.
claims.quote: Results showed that exposure to manipulated Instagram photos directly led to lower body image.

claims.text: Girls with higher social comparison tendencies are negatively affected by exposure to manipulated photos.
claims.quote: Especially, girls with higher social comparison tendencies were negatively affected by exposure to the manipulated photos.

claims.text: Body image was significantly more negative after viewing thin media images than after viewing images of either average size models, plus size models, or inanimate objects.
claims.quote: Body image was significantly more negative after viewing thin media images than after viewing images of either average size models, plus size models, or inanimate objects.

claims.text: The negative effect of thin media images on body image was stronger for participants less than 19 years of age.
claims.quote: This effect was stronger for between-subjects designs, participants less than 19 years of age, and for participants who are vulnerable to activation of a thinness schema.

claims.text: Internalization of body shape ideals is strongly linked to body dissatisfaction in younger individuals.
claims.quote: IBSI and body dissatisfaction were strongly linked: (a) in younger individuals (general attractiveness-ideal internalization);

verdict: The evidence consistently shows that exposure to thin or manipulated beauty ideals on social media leads to lower body satisfaction, especially among adolescents.
caveat: While body-positive content shows promise in improving mood and satisfaction in the short term, its influence on social comparison remains limited.
caption:
Scrolling through idealized bodies changes your internal map of yourself.

Research shows that exposure to manipulated Instagram photos directly lowers body satisfaction in girls aged 14–18, especially for those who compare themselves to others. While body-positive content may improve mood in the short term, its influence on social comparison remains limited.
